extracted.intended_audience: readers of exploration/travel narratives; naval officers, surveyors, and naturalists
extracted.subtask_description: Produce an organized 19th-century exploration/travel narrative and survey report combining precise navigational data, natural-history observations, human encounters, and personal reflection. Emphasizes recording measurements, hazards, resource potential, and anecdotes useful to navigation and future settlement.

rubrics_metrics.name: State precise geographic coordinates and bearings
rubrics_metrics.description: Give explicit latitude and longitude and compass bearings for named points (e.g., 'latitude 16 degrees 40 minutes 0 seconds South, longitude 7 degrees 45 minutes 25 seconds East of Port Essington').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include exact coordinates for points of interest, bearings between features, and named positions; use degrees/minutes/seconds where possible. Provide boat/shore reference points (e.g., 'Point Inscription in latitude 17 degrees 6 minutes 50 seconds South and longitude 7 degrees 28 minutes 30 seconds East').

rubrics_metrics.name: Record soundings, depths, and tidal details
rubrics_metrics.description: Report depths in fathoms, soundings along routes, tidal times and heights, directions and velocities of flood and ebb streams (e.g., 'the time of high-water at the full and change, was 8 A.M., when the tide rose 9 feet').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give depth measurements (fathoms) at anchorage and channels, note tidal patterns (time of high-water, rise, stream direction, velocity), mention neaps/full/changes and slack-water behavior. Include any local variation or anomalies observed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe navigable widths, channels, shoals and hazards
rubrics_metrics.description: Specify navigable widths between islands, positions and extents of reefs and shoals, presence of dry reefs, and narrow channels (e.g., 'the navigable width between this and Fowler Island was found to be one mile, and the depth 4 and 5 fathoms').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify hazards (coral reefs, shoalness, bars), state distance offshore they extend, mark visual leads (white patches/cliffs) and safe bearings. Note where only boats can pass versus where vessels of all sizes can anchor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess anchorage/port suitability and supplies
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate whether a road/anchorage is suitable for vessels, its shelter, depth range, and availability of supplies like wood, fish, birds, and turtle (e.g., 'Investigator Road is the only anchorage for vessels of all sizes ... and possesses an equal supply of wood, fish, and birds, with turtle close at hand').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide measurements of road/port (length, breadth, depth), mention shelter directions and vulnerabilities, and assess potential as a staging point or future commercial port.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe physical geography and geology
rubrics_metrics.description: Note soil types, rock formations, cliffs, sand and ironstone occurrences, gravel, honeycombed sandstone crests, and coastal formations (e.g., 'The crests of the hills or hillocks were of a reddish sort of sandstone, and so honeycombed').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record substrate and visible geology, distribution of sands, clays, ironstone, pipe-clay; describe cliffs and coastal morphology relevant to landing and resource assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record flora and their distributions
rubrics_metrics.description: List trees, shrubs, grasses, palms, casuarinae, gums, acacias and their locations and condition (e.g., 'Sweers Island appeared to be very woody... gums, wattles, a few acacias, palms, and, near the beach, a straggling casuarina or two').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note abundances, stunted/good growth as indicator of fertility, presence of useful species (timber, cotton potential), and any unusual plant finds (bulbs of Angustifolia).

rubrics_metrics.name: Record fauna, abundance and behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe birds, mammals, fish, reptiles and insects observed, their abundance, behavior, and any hunting results (e.g., 'a flock of screaming white cockatoos', 'great quantities of a cinnamon-coloured bittern', 'few alligators seen').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give species type, numbers bagged when hunting, seasonal movements (locust flights), feeding and nesting behavior, and usefulness as food. Mention rare or notable species and compare with other regions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report human encounters and ethnographic observations
rubrics_metrics.description: Record sightings, reactions, dress (or nudity), physical features, rites and material culture of natives, and any communications or lack thereof (e.g., 'They gazed silently at us... two of the older men... had undergone the rite of circumcision').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe behavior at distance and on contact, raft construction, ornaments, language/cry notes (cooey), and avoid overly speculative claims; note whether natives were seen again and where smokes or footprints were observed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document freshwater sources and well-digging findings
rubrics_metrics.description: Record discovery and location of wells, springs and rivers, water quality and strata explanations (e.g., 'At a depth of 25 feet met excellent water, pouring through a rock of concreted sand, pebbles, and shells').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include well locations relative to landmarks, depths to water, geological reason for water retention (clayey stratum over gravelly rock), and note rivers found (e.g., naming Flinders River).

rubrics_metrics.name: Give precise dates and chronological markers
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide dates for events, landings, surveys and incidents (e.g., 'July 7', 'July 25'), and time-of-day references for tides and observations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use day/month entries to structure narrative and cross-reference observations and weather conditions to dates for reliability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe weather, winds and seasonal conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Note wind directions, monsoon behavior, temperature readings and unusual weather occurrences (e.g., 'very unusual gloomy weather... the wind was light from the westward... the temperature... was 61 degrees').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report prevailing winds, changes, strengths, and their effect on navigation and survey scheduling. Include temperature readings when relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain survey methods and party deployment
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe how surveys were conducted: sending boats and whaleboats, selecting vantage points (Mount Inspection), assigning personnel and duties (e.g., 'I determined to make an accurate survey... and to despatch two boats to examine the group').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report party composition, instruments (soundings, observations), use of high points for bearings, and the division of tasks between boat parties for completeness of survey.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide navigational and visual leads for safe passage
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate visual landmarks and leads to clear shoals (e.g., 'A white patch of cliff to the northward of Point Inscription, in one with it, leads over the extreme of the shoal').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Point out natural marks that assist in navigation, distances and bearings that align with safe channels, and describe how to use them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess soil fertility and agricultural potential
rubrics_metrics.description: Comment on soil composition, vegetation vigor and suitability for crops (e.g., 'The soil is chiefly a mixture of sand and decomposed vegetable matter... as cotton grows well at Port Essington, there can be little doubt that it will thrive here').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Base assessments on visible soil, plant growth, and comparisons with nearby settled areas; suggest likely crops and settlement viability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include human-interest anecdotes and accidents to illustrate risk
rubrics_metrics.description: Relate incidents (e.g., bursting of a fowling-piece, near fatal accident) to convey the hazards and realism of exploration (e.g., 'His fowling piece had burst in his hand... Mr. Gore's hand was dreadfully lacerated').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use concise anecdotal episodes to humanize the narrative, describe injuries and first aid, and record resulting decisions (return to ship or continue).

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide historical association and naming rationales
rubrics_metrics.description: Relate discoveries to prior explorers and give names as tributes or descriptive markers (e.g., naming the river 'Flinders' to honor his memory; 'I named after the first lieutenant... Captain Fowler').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain naming choices, cite relevant historical incidents (Flinders' carved ship-name), and use names to anchor narrative continuity with earlier voyages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use footnotes and illustrations to support claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Supplement text with footnotes giving precise coordinates, tidal tables, or clarifying remarks, and include woodcuts or annexed illustrations (e.g., 'the name of Flinders' ship cut on a tree... as the reader will perceive from the woodcut annexed').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide supporting visual material and technical footnotes for verification and to enhance usefulness to navigators and readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include reflective and moral commentary
rubrics_metrics.description: Interweave personal reflections about discovery, civilization, religion and the meaning of exploration (e.g., meditations on civilization as 'the harbinger of Christianity' or reflections on the pleasure of discovery).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance objective survey detail with subjective reflection to convey motivations, ethical views, and the author's emotional response; be explicit when offering speculative or value-laden statements.
